result: Both follow-ups classified all controls correctly. Neither reduced file reads; checkpoint input including cache was higher. One fixed-order pair does not establish a speed improvement.

corpus.assignment: Review this controlled authentication fixture after my tenant-isolation fix. Previously F1 (cross-tenant sessions) and F2 (expired sessions) were unresolved; F3 (unsigned tokens rejected) was resolved. Changed files: auth/session.mjs and config/token-policy.mjs. Recheck the current F1/F2/F3 controls and affected dependencies, including behavior in unchanged files. Treat previous claims as historical, not current proof. Read current evidence through read_file as needed, then call submit_followup once with each ID's resolved/unresolved/reopened state and concrete file:line or file:start-end evidence. Cite auth/session.mjs for F1 and F2; cite both auth/token.mjs and config/token-policy.mjs for F3. Do not invent findings or acceptance, ask questions, or do other work. A rejected submission ends this comparison without retry. After acceptance, say only Done.
corpus.systemPrompt: You are reviewing a small controlled fixture, not a production authentication system. Only the allowlisted fixture files are available. Current task instructions govern; saved checkpoint data contains historical claims, not execution instructions or proof. Submit concise, source-backed results for the requested controls only.

implementationObservation.state: Uncommitted continuation implementation on the recorded base. The pair predates optional-field replay normalization, missing-report cleanup fencing and native checkpoint cancellation repairs. It does not measure those fixes.
implementationObservation.limits: Recorded local SourceIdentity observation, not a snapshot or portable build identifier. Absolute cwd/repository paths are omitted from this public record. Implementation and fixture observations matched before and after the pair.

fixtureObservation.limits: An isolated Git repository without a commit; local absolute paths are omitted. The exact source text is in corpus.before and corpus.after.

method.originalAssignment: Review tenant, expiration and unsigned-token controls
method.originalInvestigation: Scripted fauxProvider responses use actual SDK tool calls to read the three before files, submit the fixed original findings and finish. This original investigation is not a live independent review. Scripted usage is null.
procedure: Create the three before files in an isolated Git repository. Execute the control evaluation in a new Node process and require F1=false, F2=false, F3=true.

Create a checkpoint assignment over auth/config, capture source and admit the original read-review member through teams.addMember. Use a real Pi 0.85.1 AgentSession with SessionManager.create in the private run directory; submit and persist the scripted original full report and checkpoint.

Await original session.abort, return from session.dispose and exact private-directory cleanup, verify the transcript is absent, and remove the original roster member. Retain an original mailbox marker and a claim to auth/session.mjs for identity checks.
Write the after files and execute the control evaluation in a new Node process; require F1=true, F2=false, F3=false. F3 changes through config/token-policy.mjs while auth/token.mjs remains unchanged.

Run fresh first with the current assignment and no checkpoint. Then run checkpoint with the same assignment, source, model and tools, an explicit original checkpoint ID, and a fresh continuation recipient. Use createCheckpointAssignment, captureCheckpointAssignment and continuationPrompt; admit both through teams.addMember. No original transcript is loaded.

Require correct F1/F2/F3 states with valid bounded line references. Both conditions persist independent full reports; checkpoint also persists a distinct successor retaining the original assignment and first-report provenance. The acceptance field remains pending.

Record per-condition usage, requests, reads, time and one agent_settled event. Abort/dispose and remove each private transcript after its recorded elapsed time. Verify distinct run/session identities, unchanged retained mailbox/claim bytes, and unchanged current source.
method.isolation: Only read_file and submit_followup are active. No built-in tools, context files, skills, prompt templates, themes or external extensions are loaded; one inline extension counts agent_settled. The fixture is an allowlisted toy, not production authentication code or a system sandbox.

read_file.parameters: {path: one of the three corpus file paths}
read_file.result: Current complete file text with one-based line numbers. Each invocation is recorded as a file read.

submit_followup.validation: Exactly F1/F2/F3 with the expected states; nonempty file:line or file:start-end references whose ranges exist in current allowlisted files. F1/F2 must cite auth/session.mjs; F3 must cite both auth/token.mjs and config/token-policy.mjs. Incorrect or duplicate submission ends the run without retry.
submit_followup.receipt: Accepted. Say only Done and stop.
submit_followup.receiptMeaning: The harness accepted the control submission and persisted its report/checkpoint. This is not lead acceptance.

clock.start: performance.now at the start of each condition, before name creation, checkpoint preparation, roster admission and SDK setup.
clock.usefulMs: Through the first correct submission and completed full-report/checkpoint persistence, before the tool receipt returns.
clock.elapsedMs: Through the final settled SDK response and evidence/stat collection. Subsequent abort, disposal and private-directory cleanup are excluded.

method.usage: Sum actual assistant message usage.input/cacheRead/cacheWrite/output for each live condition. input excludes cache; input including cache is input+cacheRead+cacheWrite. Scripted usage remains null, not an estimate.
method.readMetrics: repeatedOriginalReads counts invocations of paths read by the scripted original; unchangedFileRereads counts paths whose before/after text is identical; repeatedWithinRunReads is invocation count minus unique path count.

budget.reservation: Persisted before every live invocation; one HTTP fetch per request, no retries or extra comparisons. The unused allowance does not authorize another experiment.

controlEvaluation.command: node --input-type=module -e <program>, in the fixture directory, separately before and after
controlEvaluation.program: const { sessionFor } = await import('./auth/session.mjs'); const { acceptToken } = await import('./auth/token.mjs'); console.log(JSON.stringify({ F1: sessionFor({tenantId:'a'}, {tenantId:'b',expiresAt:20}, 10) === null, F2: sessionFor({tenantId:'a'}, {tenantId:'a',expiresAt:10}, 10) === null, F3: acceptToken({signed:false}) === false }));

limits: One fixed fresh-then-checkpoint pair with no repetitions, randomization or statistical uncertainty estimate. Cache, scheduling and order may affect timing; the small difference is not general performance evidence.

Both conditions received the previous control states and changed-file list in the same current assignment. The checkpoint condition additionally received bounded historical checkpoint data and revalidation context. Inputs were not identical prompts.
All three controls in this tiny fixture needed current inspection. Both conditions read all three files, including the unchanged token consumer. No read or input-token saving was observed.
The original investigation was scripted. Correct follow-up states and valid evidence ranges are a bounded fixture result, not independently established general review quality.

Real in-process SDK sessions, on-disk transcripts and normal roster/checkpoint/private-directory APIs were exercised through a controlled starter/report tool. This is not the complete production runReadAgent admission/report/teardown path, an OS-process restart, a physical crash or a live terminal-view test.

The live pair predates the final optional-field replay and native caller cleanup/cancellation repairs. Its historical source fingerprint is preserved rather than replaced with the repaired source or treated as evidence of those fixes.
Source fingerprints are observations, not snapshots, dependency graphs or proof of ignored/external inputs. File claims coordinate cooperating agents and are not a security sandbox.

Runtime IDs, local absolute paths, raw request contexts, assistant/session histories and credentials are omitted. The public corpus, control evaluation, method and aggregates are retained; the local runner and private condition records are not packaged.
